summary_hint: <account_holder> deposited <deposit_total> (<cash_amount> cash / <checks_total> checks) to <financial_institution> acct …<last4> on <deposit_date> via <deposit_channel>.

typed_core.name: financial_institution_name
typed_core.why: identity: which bank — matches the slip to the borrower's verified account/statement

typed_core.name: branch_identifier
typed_core.why: identity / disambiguator: which branch — helps distinguish accounts and locate the teller record

typed_core.name: account_holder_name
typed_core.why: identity: whose account received the deposit; matches to the borrower

typed_core.name: account_number_masked
typed_core.why: PII (restricted, already registered as account_number_masked): the destination account — the key that ties the deposit to a verified asset account
typed_core.prompt_hint: Slips show the account as full, last-4, or ****1234 — always file under account_number_masked; never let a full number reach the catch-all

typed_core.name: account_type
typed_core.why: disambiguator: checking vs savings — asset-eligibility context

typed_core.name: deposit_date
typed_core.why: processor: when the deposit posted — the date matched against the bank-statement credit

typed_core.name: deposit_channel
typed_core.why: disambiguator: teller / ATM / mobile / mail — affects how the deposit is corroborated and its risk

typed_core.name: transaction_or_teller_number
typed_core.why: identity / processor: the transaction reference for matching to the bank statement line

typed_core.name: deposit_total
typed_core.why: processor: the headline deposited amount — reconciled to the bank statement and to source docs

typed_core.name: cash_amount
typed_core.why: processor: cash portion — cash deposits require sourcing; the single most underwriting-relevant split
typed_core.prompt_hint: Report cash_amount, checks_total, and less_cash_received separately — do not collapse into the total

typed_core.name: checks_total
typed_core.why: disambiguator for deposit_total: the checks portion that, with cash, explains the total composition

typed_core.name: less_cash_received
typed_core.why: disambiguator for deposit_total: cash taken back reduces the net credited amount — without it the net deposit is misread

typed_core.name: currency
typed_core.why: disambiguator: non-USD deposits change the sourced amount

typed_core.name: funds_availability_date
typed_core.why: processor: when funds became usable — relevant to cash-to-close timing

typed_core.name: teller_validation_or_stamp
typed_core.why: processor: the bank validation/stamp is what makes the slip credible evidence vs a filled-in blank
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the teller validation / bank stamp verbatim — describe it, do not judge sufficiency

typed_core.name: deposit_time
typed_core.why: disambiguator: distinguishes two same-day deposits to the same account

typed_core.name: document_issue_date
typed_core.why: processor: slip date when distinct from deposit_date

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity: links the slip to the loan file, when stated (confidential)

nested_lists.name: check_items
nested_lists.shape_reason: deposited checks genuinely repeat (a slip can itemize several checks, each with payer/amount/check-number), and per-check sourcing is exactly the underwriting use ('source each item'). Flat rows {payer_or_drawer, amount, check_number, source} are light and sufficient

fields.name: payer_or_drawer
fields.why: processor: per-item sourcing — who wrote the deposited check

fields.name: amount
fields.why: processor: per-item amount that composes the checks total

fields.name: check_number
fields.pii_note: a check number is quasi-PII (ties to a drawer's account); the nested record needs its own redactor so it is not stored raw

fields.name: source
fields.why: processor: the documented source of the item — the per-item sourcing use

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date, document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: a deposit slip is a bank form, not a standardized/versioned form a rule reads

rejected.name: issuer_name, issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: the bank is captured by financial_institution_name; other contact detail has no consumer

rejected.name: effective_date, expiration_date, statement_period_start, statement_period_end
rejected.reason: a slip is a point-in-time record; deposit_date covers it, no coverage period

rejected.name: property_address, account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: not present on a deposit slip; keyed by account + transaction number

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: a slip is not executed/notarized; the depositor mark is deposit_slip_signature_or_initials (no consumer)

rejected.name: deposit_slip_signature_or_initials
rejected.reason: OPTIONAL; a depositor's initials on a slip have no rule/processor consumer

rejected.name: memo_or_description
rejected.reason: OPTIONAL free text with no consumer; catch-all captures it

encoding_variations: Net vs gross: deposit_total, cash_amount, checks_total, and less_cash_received interrelate — the credited amount is cash + checks − less_cash_received; carry all four or the net deposit is ambiguous
Account masking: slips show the account variously as full, last-4, or ****1234 — always file under account_number_masked; never let a full number reach the catch-all
Date vs time: two same-day deposits are distinguished only by deposit_time and/or transaction_or_teller_number — keep both
Validation: a machine-printed teller stamp vs a hand-written slip changes evidentiary weight — capture teller_validation_or_stamp verbatim

open_questions.q: No rule consumes this document today (Tier 3, rule_count 0). The likely future consumer is a large-deposit / asset-sourcing rule (the AS-family analog).
options: trim to amount + date + account if no rule materializes
open_questions.recommendation: keep the composition + check-items fields so that rule can be built without re-extraction

open_questions.q: check_items PII — check-item rows carry check numbers and drawer names.
options: build the nested record with a redactor (like transactions)
leave check numbers to the catch-all
open_questions.recommendation: build the nested record with a redactor rather than leaving check numbers to the catch-all; confirm the redaction approach GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: currency, deposit_time degraded (no coercer for currency_code/time).
open_questions.recommendation: degrade to str; add coercers only if a rule needs currency math or sub-day ordering

notes: This slip is sourcing evidence for a deposit on a bank statement — extract the amount, composition (cash vs checks), destination account, and date so a processor can match it.
Itemize deposited checks in check_items (payer/drawer, amount, check number) when shown; a check number is PII — keep it in the nested record with a redactor, not the catch-all.
account_number_masked reuses the existing registered _PII_FIELDS key (pre_masked true).
